description.p: Jelly is a native client for Jellyfin media servers. It plays every file as it is with mpv, so the server never has to transcode: MKV, 10-bit HEVC, AV1, Opus, FLAC, styled ASS subtitles with their fonts and PGS subtitles all play directly, with hardware decoding.

ul.li: Continue Watching, Next Up and what's new in each library
Resumes where you left off on any device, and reports what you watch back to Jellyfin
Skips intros and recaps, and counts down to the next episode over the credits
Picks audio and subtitle tracks by your Jellyfin language settings
Requests what isn't in the library yet through Seerr, and shows how its download is going
A command line for keyboard shortcuts and launchers

screenshot.caption: Home, with what's new and what you're watching

ul.li: A button for the previous episode
A show's audio and subtitles carry over to its other episodes, and switching the audio to another language turns on subtitles
Skip Outro, then a countdown to the next episode, with Play Now and Cancel
A simpler seek bar, whose time follows the pointer
A and S open the audio and subtitle menus
Linux: Jelly installed with install.sh updates itself
Fixes for subtitles after a seek, the Skip Intro button's colors, and the player's keys right after it opens
Windows: a setup that installs Jelly and keeps it up to date
Jelly says when there's a new release
Tab completion in bash, zsh and fish, including the movies and shows on your server
Signing in with a password signs in to Seerr too
Windows: the folder shows only jelly.exe and a runtime folder, and the app uses the graphics card's own OpenGL driver instead of Mesa's
